title: Investigation quickstart
summary: Follow one repository from an exact revision through typed work, terminal evidence, and finalization.
audience: A contributor making their first change to Attune or calling its MCP tools for the first time.

claims.text: Begin with repository materialization. The request names the remote, revision, invocation, and optional investigation identity; the runtime resolves that request into an investigation instead of letting later tools operate on an arbitrary path.
Keep the returned investigation and snapshot identities together. They are the stable coordinates used by later operations and by receipt inspection.
Operations run through the investigation service boundary. An operation-specific request retains its own input and result relationship instead of widening into a generic JSON handler.
Treat the terminal receipt as durable evidence of what ran. Success, failure, and cancellation remain distinct outcomes, and retained artifacts point back to the invocation that produced them.
Finalization is a lifecycle transition, not filesystem cleanup by convention. It closes the active investigation boundary and returns the final manifest for inspection.
